entries.statement: Public Paseo and dashboard status compare the owned running host executable with the contract Node and report the Node restart requirement and existing explicit provision remedy without changing the host.

target.rationale: This pure observation compares the owned executable with the selected product Node and supplies the shared restart-required result.
The public Paseo status owner merges owned process facts with the Node comparison without starting or reconfiguring the host.
Dashboard host observation presents the same contract-versus-owned-executable comparison under its read-only deadline.
The presentation boundary names the existing explicit provision command when Node restart is required.

entries.disposition: implemented and verified by focused evidence; independent verification pending

scope.applicability: Both public status paths observing a configured owned running host.
conditions: Compare the observed executable with the absolute contract Node path, even when the new target is already installed.
A matching or unobserved executable alone supplies no Node restart reason.
exclusions: Status does not install, restart, change settings or remove process records.

admission.justification: The public observation and transition boundaries together prevent an installation or status read from unexpectedly replacing a running host; focused tests demonstrate the exact mismatch and preserved-file behavior.

memberships.basis: A verified build Node, visible restart requirement and explicit retained-file transition are needed together to make the host lifecycle safe to operate.

proofs.facet: Both public status paths show an earlier executable mismatch even with the contract target present; a matching executable has no restart reason, and neither observation mutates files, settings or the host.

entries.statement: An install defers a live-host Node transition and explicit provision restarts on the contract Node, reports the observed earlier product Node folder as no longer used by that host, and preserves its files.

target.rationale: The transition owner defers install restarts, captures the observed earlier Node folder, and reports it only after explicit provision starts the replacement host.
This report-only boundary accepts only an earlier sibling product Node folder and names it as unused by this host without deleting files.
The install admission owner detects a live executable mismatch before Node acquisition or home mutations.

entries.disposition: implemented and verified by focused evidence; independent verification pending

scope.applicability: Install and explicit terminal provision when an owned running host uses an earlier product Node.
conditions: Install defers before Node or home writes.
Only a successful explicit provision restart reports the earlier sibling Node folder as unused by this host.
exclusions: No deletion of old Node files or claim that another process no longer uses them.
No automatic transition through dashboard start or status.

admission.justification: The public observation and transition boundaries together prevent an installation or status read from unexpectedly replacing a running host; focused tests demonstrate the exact mismatch and preserved-file behavior.

memberships.basis: A verified build Node, visible restart requirement and explicit retained-file transition are needed together to make the host lifecycle safe to operate.

proofs.facet: Install defers the live Node mismatch before mutation; explicit provision restarts once, reports the earlier folder as unused, retains its marker, and the next provision changes nothing.

fields.statement: The host uses the absolute product Node26.11.1 on Linux x86_64 with /proc, verifies the official archive digest before unpacking, and refuses other platforms or a foreign target.
fields.applicability: Every host acquisition and every process that starts the host: the provision's npm run, PaseoCli calls and the bridge.
conditions: The platform is Linux x86_64 with /proc; the archive URL and SHA-256 come from the contract.
The managed Node lies beside the product's python and paseo folders; the archive cache is under the user's cache folder.
exclusions: A Node already on the machine is never used for the host, whatever its version.
No install outside the product's data and cache folders, no bin link, no PATH, shell or npm-config change.
The Eve application keeps its own separate Node line.

fields.title: One build-owned host lifecycle
fields.guarantee: One build's install brings exactly that build's host — its release, its complete package lock, its plugin and a Node the product fetches and verifies itself — every dashboard start makes sure that host runs, one installation-wide authority names it, and neither the install nor a dashboard start or stop removes a host that is running. Release changes stay build-owned; when a required live-host transition is needed — a different contract, or a same-contract listen, start-only-setting, Node or package change — the explicit terminal provision (`agents-remember paseo provision --config <file>`) performs it, and a different build is not a necessary condition for that transition. Public status exposes an observed executable mismatch with the contract Node and its existing explicit provision remedy without changing the host; successful explicit provision reports the earlier sibling product Node folder as no longer used by that host while retaining its files.

fields.context: The host build must move from its old Node pin to the current release while the operational witness distinguishes a Node failure from an unrelated startup tool gap.

alternatives.option: Select the newest Node26 release for the host build.
alternatives.reason: The developer selected the current line; the sandbox host and bridge work on26 and an offered Pi agent replies. The same native startup refusal occurs on the matched22 control.

alternatives.option: Select the newest Node24 release if the host fails on26.
alternatives.reason: The authorized fallback requires a failure attributable to the host on26; the matched startup gap supplies no such evidence.
alternatives.reconsider_when: A controlled witness establishes that the host fails on26 and the failure is absent on the matched control.

alternatives.option: Keep Node22 if both selected newer lines fail.
alternatives.reason: Retaining the previous line is only the packet fallback after both newer host attempts fail; no such failure occurred.
alternatives.reconsider_when: Both authorized newer Node host attempts fail with retained attributable evidence.

consequences: The packaged contract pins26.11.1 and its verified archive. A common startup tool refusal does not activate24. Provisioning the developer installation remains a separate post-landing action owned by the Architect.
fields.decider: Developer D113, quoted in DEVELOPER-DIRECTION.md; approved MIK-R107@v1 current66 witness/control amendment.

admission.justification: The selected current Node line and the evidence condition for using24 constrain later runtime changes; an unrelated native tool gap must not silently select an older runtime.
